turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Mehta, I checked you before the doctor calls. Blood pressure is 138 over 86, pulse 78, temperature 36.8, and oxygen saturation 98 percent. Please sit, he will be in shortly.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arjun, come in, and your wife too, please. I am all ears. What has been going on with you?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing, doctor, truly. Same old headache only. She has made a full drama and dragged me here.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is not the same, doctor. For years it was his migraine, but this past month he wakes up with the pain, and he has been vomiting with it.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Arre, don't exaggerate na. Vomiting happened twice, that is all, not every day. Morning headache, maybe a little, I don't know, it goes after tea.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hmm, I want to hear it properly. Arjun, how long have these headaches actually been with you?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Since college, so twenty years, more or less. It is migraine. It comes, I take a tablet, I carry on with work. I am fine.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The old ones, yes. But the new morning pattern, sorry, I said one month just now, it is closer to three weeks. Three weeks he is worse on waking.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Three weeks is also too much. Maybe, um, ten days. It is not a big thing, doctor.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the timing is a bit unclear, somewhere between ten days and three weeks. When it comes in the morning, what does the pain actually feel like?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Throbbing, same as always, left side. Light bothers me a bit. I lie down for some time and it eases. Nothing new in it.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he is snoring like anything these days, the whole night, and in the daytime he is so tired he dozes off on the sofa. He will never admit it.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): I do not snore. And I am not tired. I work the full day, I am perfectly okay. She worries for no reason.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, I am holding both versions for a moment. Any vomiting today, any fever, or any weakness in an arm or a leg?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever, no weakness, and the vomiting was not today. Last time was Sunday, and once before that, so twice only.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): What about double vision, any fit, confusion, or pain in the neck?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No, none of that. Vision is fine. I am telling you, it is the usual migraine, nothing else.
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He did say the light was hurting, and once he felt a bit sick in the car. But no, he has not had any fit, that much is true.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me what medicines you are actually taking for the headache.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Sumatriptan, fifty milligrams, when the headache starts. Maybe twice a week. And Crocin, paracetamol, one gram, if it is mild. I don't need much.

[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Twice a week? Arjun, you have been taking the sumatriptan almost every morning this month, I have seen the strips. And the Crocin also, two or three times in a day, not just sometimes.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): Those strips are old ones, she is counting old strips. I take fifty mg by mouth, only when I need it. Not every day. Please, doctor.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other regular tablets, for pressure or sugar or anything?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No, nothing regular. I am not a tablet person at all.

[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His father takes metformin for his diabetes, five hundred mg, but that is my father-in-law, not Arjun. And my sister takes biotin for her hair, that one is also not his.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, we will keep those separate, they are not yours. Any allergy to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): No allergies. Nothing.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Wait, when he was small his mother said penicillin gave him a rash. He has avoided it since then. He always forgets to mention.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): That is some old story from childhood. I don't even remember a rash. I have taken so many antibiotics. There is no allergy, forget it.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will note that you two don't agree, and we will be careful with penicillin anyway. Do you smoke, or take alcohol?
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't smoke. Alcohol only at weddings, one peg, very rare. I work in accounts, a sitting job, not much exercise.
[SEG0032] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He quit smoking six years back, actually. He says he doesn't smoke, but he used to, about ten a day.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, let me look at you quickly. Follow my finger, pupils are equal and reacting to light. There is no stiffness in the neck.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Now squeeze my fingers, and push up with both feet. Power is normal on both sides. Touch your nose for me, coordination is fine, and I am not seeing any weakness.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): See, everything is normal only. Can we finish? I have a client call at four, this is eating my afternoon.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Almost. The back of the eyes looks clear, no swelling of the disc that I can make out. Walk to the door and back, gait is steady.

[SEG0037] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor, sorry to interrupt, his weight today is 92 kilos and height is 172 centimetres, if you want them. He said the cuff felt tight, so the blood pressure I told you was the repeat reading.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that helps. Arjun, with this newer morning pain and the vomiting, I was going to book an MRI of the brain for this week.
[SEG0039] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, please book it. I have been saying something is not right. Also he grinds his teeth at night, but that one is old.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Teeth grinding is just tension from the office, for years, not a disease. And I don't want any scan. Waste of money. The headache is the same migraine I have always had.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I understand you feel it has not changed. Morning headache with vomiting is still a pattern I don't like to wave away. Your examination, though, is reassuring.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Actually, let me change that plan. I will not book the MRI today. We might do the scan if the morning headaches and the vomiting do not settle in two weeks.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Two weeks, fine. It will settle, it always settles. I don't even think we need to come back.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I would still like to see you in two weeks, whether it has settled or not, so we can decide properly. The visit itself is fixed. The scan is only if things are not better.
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And what about the snoring and the tiredness? Could it be some sleep problem? My brother has sleep apnea and he uses a machine at night.
[SEG0046] person_3 (PATIENT): Her brother is a different case, he is very obese and all. I am not tired, I do not snore, I don't have that. Please don't start a new topic.

[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am not saying it is sleep apnea. That is one possibility I cannot rule out, along with a change in your migraine, or, less likely, something structural, given the morning vomiting. The scan stays a maybe, only if this does not settle.
[SEG0048] person_3 (PATIENT): Migraine, that is all it is. You can write migraine. The other things are just theory, doctor.

[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): On the sumatriptan, please don't take it every day even if the strips are in the drawer. Keep fifty milligrams for a clear attack, not more than two days in a week. Paracetamol one gram, maximum three times a day, not beyond that.
[SEG0050] person_3 (PATIENT): Three times, okay okay. I already don't take that much. Sumatriptan twice a week is what I do. She just worries too much.

[SEG0051] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, the paracetamol, sometimes he takes two tablets of 650, not the one gram. I have seen both boxes at home, Crocin 650 and the one gram. I am not sure which he finishes more.
[SEG0052] person_3 (PATIENT): Mostly the one gram. The 650 box is her sister's, I think, for period pain or something. I don't take that one.

[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then we leave the sister's tablets completely out of this. For you, Arjun, when you take paracetamol, stick to one gram. I had been thinking of starting propranolol as a preventive, but with the picture still not clear I will not start it today.
[SEG0054] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His mother had migraine also, quite bad. She used to take some blue tablet, I never knew the name of it.
[SEG0055] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, mother's migraine, half the family has something. The tablet name, who remembers. It doesn't change my case.

[SEG0056] person_2 (DOCTOR): A family tendency does fit your long history. I am not ordering any blood tests today. If the vomiting becomes daily, or you get weakness, new confusion, or a sudden thunderclap pain, come straight to emergency, don't wait out the two weeks.
[SEG0057] person_1 (NURSE): I can give the two-week follow-up slip at the desk when you leave. Do you want a morning or an evening slot, doctor?

[SEG0058] person_2 (DOCTOR): Morning slot, two weeks from today. You give him the slip. Arjun, keep a small note of headache days and any vomit, and bring it along. If you are clearly better we may skip the scan, and if not, we might send you for the MRI at that visit.
[SEG0059] person_3 (PATIENT): Diary, scan, all extra work. I will come in two weeks only because she will force me. I am still telling you it is nothing.
[SEG0060] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will be there, I will make sure of it. Thank you, doctor. He slept only four hours last night, and of course he will not tell you that himself.
[SEG0061] person_2 (DOCTOR): Four hours is very little, we can pick up the sleep at the next visit. Go safely, both of you.

spec.situation: Person with long headaches who now has a different pattern (worse in the morning, or with vomiting); takes sumatriptan or paracetamol often; partner says snoring and tiredness too; patient dismisses it. Doctor does a quick neuro exam and orders a scan conditionally.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Transcript says her brother has sleep apnea, not brother-in-law.
